waypoints.name: Kaza
waypoints.advice: Kaza is where the day begins. Next is Kunzum Pass.

waypoints.name: Kunzum Pass

waypoints.name: Manali

sections.advice: Kaza → Kunzum Pass climbs about 4551 m in 56 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Kunzum Pass → Manali drops about 4551 m over 56 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

spiti-valley-circuit-kaza-manali.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Spiti Valley Circuit. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Kaza → Kunzum Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 8.1%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter — first and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding.

scenicChapters.title: Kunzum Pass → Manali
scenicChapters.narrative: 4551 m come off over 110 km at around 8.1%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

spiti-valley-circuit-kaza-manali.story: The highest point is about 5,050 m. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.title: Stadhuis → Belfort met Lakenhal
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 26 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

It crosses from Belgium into France - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. The line favours views over speed.
